transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, hello doctor. I came in because... I just keep steering clear of my own workshop. And, well, any family get-together where my brother-in-law might be, I just don't go. I guess after all this time, I'm just tired of planning my whole life around not running into those reminders. That's really why I'm here.
Are there specific things or situations that you've been avoiding?

Well, like I was just saying, it's mainly those two things. My own workshop... I just steer clear of it completely now. And then any family get-together where my brother-in-law might show up. If I know he's going to be there, I just don't go. 

Those are the main situations. I'm just getting too old to keep planning my whole life around dodging those reminders, you know?
What happened in your workshop that makes you avoid it?

Well... to be honest, doctor, I'd really rather not get into the details of exactly what happened. Not today, anyway. 

It was just... a really bad situation. I don't think I'm ready to talk about the actual event right now, if that's all right with you. I just know I can't bring myself to go back in there.
For how long have you been avoiding your workshop and family get-togethers?
Well, it's been going on since that confrontation with my brother-in-law. That was... let's see, about two years and four months ago now. Ever since then, I've just been staying away.
What happened during the confrontation with your brother-in-law?

Well... that's all tied in with the workshop. Like I said a minute ago, I really just don't want to get into the details of what happened. 

I'm sorry, doctor, I just... I'd rather not talk about the actual confrontation today, either. I just know it was bad enough that I don't want anything to do with him anymore.
Do you feel anxious or fearful when you think about going back to your workshop or encountering your brother-in-law?
No, I wouldn't call it fear. I'm not really anxious or scared about it... I just have absolutely no desire to go back in there, and I don't want to see him. It's just better if I stay away.
Do you ever have memories or thoughts about what happened in your workshop that come into your mind when you don't want them to?

Yeah, I do. Out of nowhere, I'll just... see his hand holding that heavy tool again. It's like a picture that just pops right into my head. It happens when I'm doing completely unrelated things, like shaving in the morning or when I'm working on a painting. Even after all this time, it still makes my chest tighten up when it happens.
Do you feel like avoiding your workshop and family get-togethers is interfering with your daily life or activities?

Well, I still manage to get by with the basics, you know, day-to-day stuff. But... yeah, I guess it does interfere. I used to do these regular volunteer jobs that meant I had to be in the workshop, and I've just completely stopped doing those. And I don't go to any of the big family events anymore. 

Even my painting... it's just in fits and starts now. Most of my good supplies are still out in that workshop, and since I won't go near the place, I just... I don't paint as much as I used to. So, yeah, I suppose it has changed things.
Do you have nightmares about what happened in your workshop?

Yeah, I do. Most nights I can get to bed alright, but... I either just lie there listening for noises in the house, or I'll wake up from one of those bad dreams about the workshop. And when I wake up from one of those, I'm usually just wide awake for an hour or two. It takes a good while before I can even try to go back to sleep.
Do you have difficulty concentrating on things you're trying to do?

No, not really. I mean, I can still read the paper or watch a program on TV without losing my place. My focus seems to be about the same as it's always been. I don't think I have any trouble with that.
Do you find yourself jumping or startled more easily than you used to, even by small noises or unexpected movements?
No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. I don't think I'm any more jumpy than I used to be. Small noises don't really bother me or make me startle.
Do you feel like you've become less interested in activities or things you used to enjoy?
No, I don't think so. I still like doing the same things I always have. I haven't really lost interest in my hobbies or anything like that. I still enjoy my usual routine just fine.
Do you try to push away or avoid thoughts or memories about what happened in your workshop?

Yes, I do. Honestly, that's the main reason I came in to see you. I keep steering clear of my own workshop... I just avoid it completely now. And I skip out on any family get-together where my brother-in-law might show up. After all this time, I'm just tired of having to plan my whole life around not running into those reminders.
Do you often find yourself constantly on the lookout for potential dangers or threats?

Yes, I'd say I do. Even when I'm somewhere familiar, like the senior center or down in the church basement... I find myself checking who just came in. I always make sure I know exactly where the door is, and... well, I keep checking whether anyone is standing too close behind me. I just keep an eye on things like that now.
Have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy doing?

I think you might have asked me that a few minutes ago, but... no, I haven't. Like I said before, I still like doing the same things I always have. My hobbies and my daily routine are still perfectly fine. I haven't lost any interest there.
How do you feel emotionally when those memories or thoughts about what happened in your workshop come into your mind unexpectedly?

Well, I don't really feel much of anything, to be honest. I mean, I don't get all worked up or start panicking or anything like that. When a thought like that pops into my head, I just... I just don't like it, so I push it right back out. But emotionally? No, I wouldn't say I've noticed any big reaction to it.
Do you ever feel guilty about what happened in your workshop?

Yeah, I do. I keep telling myself I should have put my foot down sooner... you know, never let him stay with us in the first place. I just think maybe none of this would have happened if I'd handled it like a man right from the start.
Have you noticed any decrease in how often you participate in or enjoy activities that were once important to you, outside of the workshop and family gatherings?

No, I wouldn't say so. Like I mentioned a minute ago, I still do the same things I've always done. My routine is pretty much the same, and I haven't stopped doing anything I usually enjoy. I just keep busy with my regular stuff.
Have you lost interest in social activities or hobbies that you used to find enjoyable?

Well, like I was just saying a second ago... no, not really. I haven't lost interest in my hobbies or seeing folks. I still do all the things I used to enjoy. That part of my life hasn't really changed at all.
